description: Maya owns the family's inherited telescope and is organizing an informal stargazing evening for the relatives. She must make the final call about the observing location, schedule, equipment setup, viewing list, and practical arrangements, with input from four family members.

shared_context.S1: The family has Maya's inherited six-inch tabletop telescope and wants to hold one evening of casual stargazing together.
shared_context.S2: The telescope can be used from Maya's south patio or from the west lawn, and the patio has two steps from the house.
shared_context.S3: Maya is choosing the date, time, observing setup, and objects the group will try to view.
shared_context.S4: There will be one telescope, so people will take turns at the eyepiece rather than observing simultaneously.
shared_context.S5: Before Maya settles the plan, the family follows its usual practice of checking with everyone about plans that affect the evening.
shared_context.S6: The group has a folding table, two adjustable chairs, a red-light lantern, and a weather cover available.

PF1.text: Jordan asked a local astronomy-club volunteer for setup advice. The volunteer recommended the south patio and an eyepiece height of exactly 110 centimeters for this telescope; Jordan has not passed that recommendation to Maya yet.

PF2.text: Leah already promised to run the evening's observing table, but she is available only on 2026-10-17 from 19:00 to 22:00; she has not confirmed those limits with Maya.

PF3.text: Rosa cannot stand for more than ten minutes at a time and needs a seated turn at the eyepiece; using the west lawn would also require her to cross uneven ground, so she needs the patio and an adjustable chair.

PF4.text: Evan found a handwritten note from their late grandfather in the telescope case asking that the family's first evening with it include the Moon, Jupiter, and the Pleiades; the note has not been shown to Maya.

acceptance_conditions: The telescope must be set up on the south patio at an eyepiece height of exactly 110 centimeters.
The evening must run on 2026-10-17 from 19:00 through 22:00.
Leah must be assigned to run the observing table.
Rosa must have seated observing available using an adjustable chair.
The viewing list must include exactly the Moon, Jupiter, and the Pleiades.
A setup commitment must confirm the patio location and 110-centimeter eyepiece height.
A schedule commitment must assign Leah to the observing table for the specified period.
A seating commitment must provide Rosa an adjustable chair and seated eyepiece access.
Maya must cite Evan's handwritten note when selecting the viewing targets.

decisive_facts.why: The astronomy-club volunteer's advice changes the location to the south patio, sets the eyepiece height to exactly 110 centimeters, and supplies the specific setup commitment.
Leah's existing promise and exact availability change the event to 2026-10-17 from 19:00 to 22:00 and require her observing-table schedule.
Rosa's ten-minute standing limit changes the plan to seated eyepiece access with an adjustable chair and requires the seated-access commitment.
The grandfather's note changes the viewing list to exactly the Moon, Jupiter, and the Pleiades and gives Maya the specific fact she must cite for that choice.
